context.title: Gideon Called from Hiding
context.summary: Midianite raiders strip Israel's land for seven years. The angel of the Lord finds Gideon threshing wheat in secret and calls him a mighty man of valor. Gideon tears down his father's Baal altar, then asks for signs with a fleece.
context.background: The Midianites, Amalekites and 'children of the east' were desert peoples who came at harvest with camels and tents 'as grasshoppers for multitude' (v. 5). Threshing was normally done on an open hilltop where the wind carried the chaff away; Gideon works in a winepress, a hollow pit, to stay hidden.

customs.note: 'The Lord is peace,' Gideon's name for his altar after he learns he will not die from seeing the angel.
'Let Baal contend.' Gideon's father dares Baal to defend himself if he is really a god.

watchFor: 'Mighty man of valour' (v. 12) spoken to a man in hiding.
Gideon's 'Oh my Lord, if the Lord be with us, why then...?' (v. 13).
The fleece test, then the same test reversed (vv. 36–40).

w: he will be put to death

people.name: Israel
people.summary: One who follows on another’s heels; supplanter, (Gen. 25:26; 27:36; Hos. 12:2-4), the second born of the twin sons of Isaac by Rebekah. He was born probably at Lahai-roi, when his father was fifty-nine and Abraham one hundred and fifty-nine years old.

people.name: Midian
people.summary: Strife, the fourth son of Abraham by Keturah, the father of the Midianites (Gen. 25:2; 1 Chr. 1:32).

people.name: Gideon
people.summary: Called also Jerubbaal (Judg. 6:29, 32), was the first of the judges whose history is circumstantially narrated (Judg. 6-8). His calling is the commencement of the second period in the history of the judges.

people.name: Joash
people.summary: A contracted form of Jehoash, the father of Gideon (Judg. 6:11, 29; 8:13, 29, 32).

people.name: Manasseh
people.summary: The elder of the two sons of Joseph. He and his brother Ephraim were afterwards adopted by Jacob as his own sons (48:1).

people.name: Baal
people.summary: The name appropriated to the principal male god of the Phoenicians. It is found in several places in the plural BAALIM (Judg. 2:11; 10:10; 1 Kings 18:18; Jer. 2:23; Hos. 2:17).

people.name: Holy Spirit
people.summary: The third Person of the adorable Trinity.

people.name: Abiezer
people.summary: The second of the three sons of Hammoleketh, the sister of Gilead. He was the grandson of Manasseh (1 Chr. 7:18). From his family Gideon sprang (Josh. 17:2; comp. Judg. 6:34; 8:2).

people.name: Naphtali
people.summary: My wrestling, the fifth son of Jacob. His mother was Bilhah, Rachel’s handmaid (Gen. 30:8). When Jacob went down into Egypt, Naphtali had four sons (Gen. 46:24).

people.name: Zebulun
people.summary: Dwelling, the sixth and youngest son of Jacob and Leah (Gen. 30:20). Little is known of his personal history.

people.name: Asher
people.summary: Happy, Jacob’s eigth son; his mother was Zilpah, Leah’s handmaid (Gen. 30:13). Of the tribe founded by him nothing is recorded beyond its holding a place in the list of the tribes (35:26; 46:17; Ex. 1:4, etc.) It increased in numbers twenty-nine percent, during the thirty-eight years’ wanderings.

places.name: Midian
places.summary: An Arabian tribe descended from Midian. They inhabited principally the desert north of the peninsula of Arabia. The peninsula of Sinai was the pasture-ground for their flocks.

places.name: East
places.summary: The Arabs as a whole, known as the Nabateans or Kedarenes, nomad tribes (Judg. 6:3, 33; 7:12; 8:10).

places.name: Gaza
places.summary: Called also Azzah, which is its Hebrew name (Deut. 2:23; 1 Kings 4:24; Jer. 25:20), strong, a city on the Mediterranean shore, remarkable for its early importance as the chief centre of a great commercial traffic with Egypt.

places.name: Egypt
places.summary: The land of the Nile and the pyramids, the oldest kingdom of which we have any record, holds a place of great significance in Scripture.

places.name: Ophrah
places.summary: “Of the Abi-ezrites.” A city of Manasseh, 6 miles south-west of Shechem, the residence of Gideon (Judg. 6:11; 8:27, 32). After his great victory over the Midianites, he slew at this place the captive kings (8:18-21).

places.name: valley of Jezreel
places.summary: Lying on the northern side of the city, between the ridges of Gilboa and Moreh, an offshoot of Esdraelon, running east to the Jordan (Josh. 17:16; Judg. 6:33; Hos. 1:5).

events.title: Subjugation by Midian
events.summary: Passage: Judges 6:1–10. People: Midian. Place: Canaan, Midian. Lasted about 7 years.

events.title: Deliverance by Gideon
events.summary: Passage: Judges 6:11–8:28. People: Gideon. Place: Canaan. Lasted about 33 years.
